defaultControlTooltips.shiftHz: Additive frequency offset used by this spectral transform.
defaultControlTooltips.scale: Frequency ratio around the selected pivot or detected peak.
defaultControlTooltips.pivotHz: Frequency reference used as a centre, anchor or fundamental.

effectHelp.controlTooltipRule: each mode-control wrapper uses the matching modes[].tooltipOverrides entry when present and otherwise uses the default control tooltip; inactive controls remain visible and disabled

controls.label: DISPLAY
controls.presentation: two layer toggles labelled WF and FFT; the last visible layer cannot be disabled

controls.label: PIVOT
controls.format: frequency with k suffix above 1000 Hz

modes.label: Neutral
modes.description: Leaves the spectral frame unchanged; Freeze and the global Mix path still apply.

modes.label: Pivot Bend
modes.description: Expands or contracts frequency distance around Center by a limited ratio; Amount also blends the transformed spectrum.

tooltipOverrides.shiftHz: Maximum pivot-centred expansion or contraction; positive values expand and negative values contract.
tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Frequency that remains fixed while surrounding frequencies bend.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Increase the bend ratio and blend toward the bent spectrum.

modes.label: Magnitude Diffusion
modes.description: Averages neighbouring bin magnitudes, smooths them over time, and retains each bin's current phase.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Blend toward the diffused spectrum and increase its averaging range.
tooltipOverrides.widthQ: Radius of neighbouring bins included in the magnitude average.

modes.label: Stereo Translate
modes.description: Translates the left and right spectra by equal Hz offsets in opposite directions; mono input uses one translation direction.

tooltipOverrides.shiftHz: Maximum opposite Hz translation applied to the two channels.

modes.label: Harmonic Sieve
modes.description: Retains bands near integer multiples of Fundamental and attenuates the gaps without boosting them.

tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Fundamental frequency used to construct the harmonic grid.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Increase attenuation between the retained harmonic bands.
tooltipOverrides.widthQ: Width of each band retained around the harmonic grid.

modes.label: Spectral Divider
modes.description: Reads stepped 1x to 4x source frequencies, dividing spectral content downward by integer ratios.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Select the integer frequency divisor and blend it with the original spectrum.

modes.label: Peak-Relative Gate
modes.description: Derives a threshold from the strongest spectral bin and attenuates bins below it.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Raise both the spectral gate threshold and the reduction below it.

modes.label: Phase Reset
modes.description: Sets the transformed branch to zero phase, then blends it with the original spectrum.

modes.label: Hz Translation
modes.description: Adds the same signed Hz offset to every frequency component, bending harmonic ratios.

tooltipOverrides.shiftHz: Frequency added to or subtracted from every spectral bin.

modes.label: Pivot Reflection
modes.description: Reflects frequency order around Reflect Axis; larger Map Scale values compress the audible output toward the axis.

tooltipOverrides.scale: Source-map slope; larger values compress output distances toward Reflect Axis.
tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Frequency axis around which the spectrum is reversed.

modes.label: Peak Repel
modes.description: Detects the strongest bin and moves the full spectrum farther from Anchor by the peak-to-anchor offset.

tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Reference frequency that the detected dominant peak moves away from.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Increase the peak-relative displacement and blend toward the repelled spectrum.

modes.label: Peak Stretch 2x
modes.description: Keeps the detected peak fixed and doubles every component's linear Hz distance from it.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Blend toward the fixed 2x peak-relative stretch.

modes.label: Peak Compress 2:1
modes.description: Keeps the detected peak fixed and halves every component's linear Hz distance from it.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Blend toward the fixed 2:1 peak-relative compression.

modes.label: Peak Stretch
modes.description: Keeps the strongest peak fixed and expands linear Hz distances by the Span control plus one.

tooltipOverrides.scale: Expansion control; the applied peak-relative factor is Span plus one.

modes.label: Peak Compress
modes.description: Keeps the strongest peak fixed and divides linear Hz distances by the Span control plus one.

tooltipOverrides.scale: Compression control; peak-relative distances are divided by Span plus one.

modes.label: Harmonic Scan
modes.description: Retains bands near integer multiples of a fundamental transposed by Scan in cents.

tooltipOverrides.shiftHz: Harmonic-grid offset in cents; small values provide fine movement.
tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Base fundamental frequency for the moving harmonic grid.
tooltipOverrides.widthQ: Width of each retained band in the harmonic grid.

modes.label: Octave Stack Tight
modes.description: Sums seven octave-related resamplings through a tight octave-periodic window.

tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Frequency anchor for the repeating octave window.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Move the seven-layer stack through one octave of resampling position.

modes.label: Octave Stack Wide
modes.description: Sums seven octave-related resamplings through a broad octave-periodic window.

tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Frequency anchor for the repeating octave window.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Move the seven-layer stack through one octave of resampling position.

modes.label: Magnitude Comb
modes.description: Applies a cosine comb to spectral magnitudes. Tooth spacing is the absolute Spacing value plus ten percent of Base.

tooltipOverrides.shiftHz: Unsigned spacing contribution; positive and negative values produce the same spacing.
tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Base frequency contributing ten percent of the mask spacing.

modes.label: Ratio Crossfade
modes.description: Crossfades complex bins between the original and pivot-scaled spectra without phase tracking.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Crossfade the complex spectrum; intermediate values can produce phase cancellation.

modes.label: Phase-Tracked Scale
modes.description: Rescales frequency distance around Pivot and applies phase tracking to remapped bins.

tooltipOverrides.scale: Frequency-distance scale around Pivot; this is not a whole-spectrum pitch ratio.

modes.label: Phase Ripple
modes.description: Applies sinusoidal frequency-dependent phase rotation; partial blending can also alter magnitude.

tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Frequency scale of the sinusoidal phase ripple; one full cycle spans about 2 pi times this value.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Increase phase rotation and blend toward the rotated spectrum.

modes.label: Band Glitch
modes.description: Randomly offsets spectral content only inside the band selected by Band Center and Band Q; Density sets event probability and wet depth.

tooltipOverrides.shiftHz: Signed source-bin offset applied when a selected spectral region glitches.
tooltipOverrides.pivotHz: Centre frequency of the spectral band eligible for glitch processing.
tooltipOverrides.amount: Probability and wet depth of random glitch events inside the selected band.
tooltipOverrides.widthQ: Quality factor for the selected band; higher values make the band narrower.

modes.label: Pitch Map
modes.description: Quantizes spectral energy toward the nearest pitch classes in the selected major or minor key. Map Depth blends the original and quantized spectra.

tooltipOverrides.amount: Blend between the original spectrum and the scale-quantized pitch map.

waterfall.timeAxis: left to right; newest frame enters at the right edge
waterfall.frequencyAxis: vertical; low frequencies at the bottom and high frequencies at the top
waterfall.historyImplementation: 4096-column by 192-bin quantised ring buffer is the source of truth; live updates use incremental canvas shifts while resize, layout and LOOK changes redraw from stored history
waterfall.visualReference: VISION is the default Vision 4X inspired profile; PULSE, PHOSPHOR and XRAY provide alternate local renderings of the same stored analyzer energy
waterfall.dataContract: uses analyzerFrame.output without changing transfer rate, point count or DSP data
waterfall.sampling: nearest transferred analyzer bin to avoid a second interpolation blur pass
waterfall.heatScale: each LOOK maps decoded stored dB values through its own floor, ceiling, gamma and ordered colour stops while preserving crisp nearest-neighbour pixels
waterfall.pixelOwnership: waterfallCanvas pixels encode analyzer energy only; parameter feedback, event markers and readout decoration must never be blended, filled or composited into the heat canvas

modeOverlays.role: restrained translucent selected-band guide rendered above, never into, waterfallCanvas
modeOverlays.formula: binWidth = Nyquist / (FFTSize / 2); bandwidthHz = clamp(pivotHz / clamp(widthQ, 0.05, 8), 4 * binWidth, Nyquist); lowHz = max(binWidth, pivotHz - bandwidthHz / 2); highHz = min(Nyquist, pivotHz + bandwidthHz / 2)
modeOverlays.dataIsolation: does not seed, recolour, blur or otherwise mutate analyzer history or analyzerFrame data

modeOverlays.role: compact text readout of the current pitchRoot and pitchScale
modeOverlays.dataIsolation: does not draw pitch energy or synthesize analyzer data

visualProfileContract.switchBehaviour: recolour the complete visible waterfall from the existing quantised dB ring history
visualProfileContract.allowedRedraw: a LOOK change may increment the full heat-canvas render count
visualProfileContract.historyMutation: LOOK changes must not seed, append, clear or reorder history and must preserve history head, history count, advance count and marker positions
visualProfileContract.processingIsolation: LOOK changes do not affect DSP, audio, latency, analyzerFrame payloads, the 15 Hz transfer, scroll speed, analyzer layout or the host parameter list
visualProfileContract.feedbackIsolation: LOOK changes do not emit parameterGesture events and do not create a waterfall parameter marker or toolbar parameter readout
visualProfileContract.overlayRule: grid accents and the newest-edge cursor may follow the selected LOOK, while guides and the dedicated parameter event track remain separate from heat-map pixels
visualProfileContract.freezeRule: LOOK may recolour stored history while HOLD is active but must not advance the timeline

acceptanceCriteria: All 14 plugin parameters are represented and use the exact IDs in this document; pitchRoot and pitchScale are appended without changing existing IDs or mode values.
Changing a WebView control updates the JUCE parameter and records a valid host automation gesture.
Host automation and state restore update the WebView without a page reload.

All 24 PROCESS values have non-empty effect descriptions; the selected description and mode-specific control tooltips update after pointer input, keyboard input, host automation and state restore without resizing the top bar.

Band Glitch keeps Pivot and Width/Q as automatable DSP parameters, labels them Band Center and Band Q, and displays their exact selected band as a restrained DOM overlay without changing waterfallCanvas pixels.
Pitch Map exposes automatable pitchRoot values C through B and pitchScale values Major and Minor; its compact selectors replace AXIS in the same five-column slot only while Pitch Map is selected.
The Pitch Map readout reflects Root and Scale without generating or modifying analyzerFrame data.
Pointer drag, keyboard adjustment and double-click reset emit a restrained knob particle trail from a fixed 24-particle pool, while host automation, initial state and restored state emit none.
The knob particle animator stops when its pool is empty, is cleared when hidden or resized, and is completely disabled by prefers-reduced-motion.

About opens as a keyboard-contained modal and presents verified openFAD, UnpureBloom, source repository, undeclared FlipShift license status, upstream openFAD GNU AGPLv3 and main-feature information without changing plugin parameters.
Native About links launch only the exact C++ allow list in the system browser; browser preview links use a separate noopener tab.

In native mode the document root is marked native-surface and disables text selection, contextmenu, dragstart/drop, overscroll, tap highlight, F5/F12 and Ctrl/Cmd browser refresh, location, source and zoom commands while preserving Tab, arrows, Enter, Space, Escape and form interaction.

Hiding the native editor stops the frontend main requestAnimationFrame loop, active gestures and knob particles while analyzer production remains enabled until Editor destruction; showing it resumes from preserved waterfall history without changing plugin parameters.
Spectrum, Waterfall and Both retain values 0, 1 and 2 and reproduce the previous WebView layout semantics.
Waterfall time moves left to right, frequency is vertical, and 1x/2x/4x/8x advance approximately 15/30/60/120 visual columns per second without changing the 15 Hz analyzerFrame transfer.
WF and FFT layer buttons preserve analyzerView values 0, 1 and 2 and never allow both analyzer layers to be hidden.

VISION, PULSE, PHOSPHOR and XRAY are visually distinct while every LOOK keeps low energy dark, high energy bright, narrow peaks crisp and nearest-neighbour sampling free of a second interpolation blur.
Pivot Bend displays shiftHz as a derived bend percentage, Harmonic Scan displays it in ct, and other modes display the raw parameter in Hz.
Inactive mode parameters remain visible and disabled rather than being removed.
Browser preview produces a deterministic nonblank waterfall in every LOOK and a secondary spectrum without regular moving diagonal bands or dark-blue slanted stripes.
Prefilled browser history and subsequent live preview columns use the same generator and do not create a visible vertical refresh boundary.

Changing DSP parameters never regenerates previous history or writes parameter graphics into the heat map; subsequent real analyzer output may affect future slices, while the marker appears only in the dedicated event track and the readout stays in the toolbar.

Changing LOOK recolours the complete visible heat map from stored dB history and may cause one full canvas render, but it preserves history head, history count, advance count, marker positions, audio, latency, analyzer transfer and the host parameter list.
Changing LOOK while HOLD is active recolours stored history without advancing the timeline, and local SPEED, LOOK and LAYOUT changes never emit parameterGesture or create parameter feedback markers.
STACK, OVERLAY and SPLIT redraw from the stored ring history and preserve the existing timeline across layout and responsive changes.

At widths up to 820px and heights up to 540px, ANALYZE/CONTROL tabs appear with ANALYZE selected by default; changing the tab emits no bridge event, parameter gesture, parameter marker or explicit waterfall-history mutation.
The document root is fixed at every supported viewport. At narrow tall sizes only parameterStrip scrolls internally; the page itself never scrolls horizontally or vertically.
No graphic logo asset is rendered or embedded until a replacement identity is approved.
The production UI loads entirely from embedded resources with no HTTP request.
Windows uses WebView2 and never the legacy Internet Explorer backend.
The UI remains usable at 1000 by 650, 621 by 844, 390 by 844, 360 by 420 and 320 by 280 without horizontal overflow or text overlap.
Breakpoints at 820/821, 620/621 and the compact 540px height boundary do not create clipped controls, page scrolling or unstable layout.
Opening, closing and reopening the editor does not duplicate event listeners or alter audio processing.
